messages:
OpsBot: alert — hosted-api endpoint /v1/generate returning 502/503 spike across region-us-west2, metric: 502_rate +43% in last 3m. link: https://grafana.example/r/alerts/903 :rotating_light:
Tara (support): seeing a handful of customer tickets reporting fast failures and timeouts. customer-prod keys show 502s, sample id: req_0a9f. forwarding to #incidents.
Mike (oncall): oncall here, assigning. Any recent rollouts?
Alyssa (eng-runtime): yes, we started a staged rollout of route-weight changes + new prefetch flag to 10% at 1750246700. I pushed the flag config to canary pool.
Jin (platform): noted. Can we check if canary selectors mis-applied to prod traffic slice?
OpsBot: deploy-notice: rollout/id=rollout-2026-11-01-17 started by alyssa at 1750246700 -> weight 10%.
Tara (support): repro steps from a customer:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"test"}' -v
response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway, body: "upstream read timeout"
Mike (oncall): collecting host logs. quick grep on gateway shows 502s returning with upstream: inference-runtime timeout waiting for response from worker pool. Looks like requests stuck waiting on kvcache warm.
Alyssa (eng-runtime): hmm prefetch flag changes adjusted kvcache prewarm window and increased prefix eviction unexpectedly for long prompts. Can cause more cache misses and longer tail latency. If canary got routed more traffic than intended, that could saturate some workers and trigger timeouts.
Jin (platform): check routing table: rollout traffic split shows slice A=90% legacy, slice B=10% new; but I see some replica tagging mismatch where regional routing used tag "canary-unscoped" and picked up additional hosts in us-west2. That explains higher local pressure.
Mike (oncall): recommendation: rollback flag in canary pool and pause rollout. Can someone run a rollback?
Alyssa (eng-runtime): I'll flip the flag and scale down the canary pool. Command:
# flip flag
redwoodctl feature unset workloads.prefetch.window --env staged --selector canary-unscoped
# scale
redwoodctl pool scale runtime-canary-us-west2 --replicas 0

Doing it now.
DeployBot: change requested by alyssa: unset workloads.prefetch.window for selector canary-unscoped. Job queued (job-8812).
OpsBot: autoscaler note: adding drain window for scaledown, may take 30-60s to reroute active connections.
Tara (support): informing affected customers: raising status page incident and telling customers we have a mitigaton in progress.
Mike (oncall): after flag unset, I'm seeing 503->downtrend. grafana: 502_rate decreased from +43% -> +8% within 60s. some residual 502s from connections getting drained.
Alyssa (eng-runtime): confirming rollout paused. I also dumped worker stacks on a troubled host and found blocked goroutines waiting on model kvcache fetch for long sequences, memory pressure spiked. We'll run a follow-up to adjust prefetch heuristics and add a guard to prevent unscoped tag selection.
Jin (platform): noted follow-ups: 1) audit selector tagging logic to prevent "canary-unscoped" from matching regional router; 2) make rollout atomic with explicit region scoping; 3) add prefetch safe-guards (max concurrent prefetch per worker).
Tara (support): tickets updated: customers notified, ETA for full recovery ETA 10m, asking for post-incident report.
Mike (oncall): rolling verification: run quick smoke against customers' tokens and internal test-suite. Example repro check:
for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -d '{"input":"short"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate; done
all 200s for 30 checks now.
DeployBot: job-8812 completed — feature unset applied, pool scaled to 0 replicas.
Alyssa (eng-runtime): creating a PR with a guardrail and a test for selector scoping. Will also open an eval to measure long-prompt cache miss penalty.
Jin (platform): I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem with action items and owners.
Mike (oncall): thumbs up. Thanks everyone. If any regression or customer escalations pop back up, @here to re-open. :thumbsup:
Tara (support): filing post-incident ticket with summary, affected customers, and support responses.
OpsBot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Closing channel thread unless new activity.
